$comment: THE ENFORCER FOR `x-banned-for-new` (Spec 122 §1.4 V7; Fold B item 2, LINK pilot 2026-08-27).
Before this file, `step.schema.json`'s `x-banned-for-new` block was METADATA WITH NO
CONSUMER — `grep -rn 'x-banned-for-new' scripts/ src/` reached nothing that read it. A
banned value was therefore banned only in prose: any new descriptor could declare
`guard: "none"`, satisfy the schema's own `guard_why` requirement, and ship. That is the
C-12 enforcement gap.
The rule is now conjunctive and BOTH halves are mandatory:
1. the sibling `*_why` the schema already requires (a justification), AND
2. an entry HERE naming the step, the exact descriptor path, the value, and the commit
that grandfathered it (an adjudication with a date and an owner).
A descriptor carrying a banned value with no entry is REFUSED by
`scripts/lib/step/validate.js assertGrandfathered`, at pipeline.step() construction —
before compute exists, and therefore before any pool is opened (Spec 122 §4.2).
ADDING AN ENTRY IS THE EXPENSIVE PATH ON PURPOSE. It is a committed, reviewed diff that
names a SHA; it is not something a descriptor can grant itself. Removing one is free.
Keys are `identity.name`. `paths` maps a descriptor path to the banned value it carries.
`rules` (added 2026-08-29, V7 GAP `no_retraction` closure) names x-banned-for-new `rules[].id`
values grandfathered for this step — used for a predicate that spans more than one field (e.g.
`no_retraction`: write_discipline.class AND retract together), which has no single `path→value`
pair to grandfather the way `paths` does. Enforced by `scripts/lib/step/validate.js
assertNoRetraction`, same construction-time refusal as `assertGrandfathered`.

link_massing.why: outputs.writes[0] (E1) is the `UPDATE parcel_buildings SET is_primary = false WHERE parcel_id = ANY($1) AND is_primary = true` that fence 5bb31faf introduced and B-8 names: it CLEARS the batch's primaries so the upsert can re-assign them without violating the partial unique index idx_parcel_buildings_one_primary (migration 081) when the primary shifts to a different building. A change guard is not merely unnecessary here, it is WRONG — `is_distinct_from` would skip exactly the rows whose primary is about to move, which is the collision the clear exists to prevent. The unguarded write is therefore the correct mechanic, and its cost is bounded and declared: `write_discipline.scope` narrows it to the batch's parcels and `idempotent_rerun: declared_drift` + `declared_drift` state that it always rewrites them.
link_massing.adjudicated_by: operator ruling 2026-08-27 (pilot 3 authorization, Fold B item 2)

link_parcel_addresses.why: outputs.writes[0] is the sole INSERT INTO parcel_address_points ... SELECT ... JOIN ST_Within ... ON CONFLICT (parcel_id, address_point_id) DO NOTHING (LG-18, class insert_only_no_retraction, retract:"none"). No column on this write target is ever updated after insert — computed_at is a write-once RUN_AT stamp. A change guard would compare a row against itself and always pass; the genuine gap IS the banned no_retraction shape itself (LPA-D1, pinned per Spec 123 §3.1 as a KNOWN-DEFECT with zero measured live exposure: an upstream geom UPDATE on parcels/address_points can leave a stale row with no repair mechanism). Both the guard axis and the retraction axis are grandfathered together here — same defect, same commit, same adjudication — mirroring link_massing's E1 precedent for the guard half (keyed on .guard, never .class, per assertGrandfathered's GUARD_PATH) and naming the rule id directly for the retraction half (per assertNoRetraction's rules[] shape, V7 GAP closure 2026-08-29).

fixture_no_retraction_allowed.why: The schema's own exemplar for the V7 grandfathered no_retraction shape — a FIXTURE, never a runnable step, exercising the rule in isolation from the guard axis (guard here is is_distinct_from, not the banned "none", so a difference in outcome between this fixture and its un-allowlisted twin can only be the rules[] allowlist). Exists so src/tests/step-schema.logic.test.ts can prove assertNoRetraction's GREEN direction is real, mirroring fixture_grandfathered_snapshot's role for assertGrandfathered.
fixture_no_retraction_allowed.adjudicated_by: Spec 124 GAP V7 no_retraction closure (schema fixture, not a manifest step)

compute_centroids.why: outputs.writes[0] is the sole conditional `UPDATE parcels SET centroid_lat=..., centroid_lng=... WHERE geom IS NOT NULL AND centroid_lat IS NULL RETURNING id` (LG-20, class write_once_backfill, retract:"none"). The WHERE clause IS the scope, not a value-change guard — an already-filled row is permanently ineligible for this step's own UPDATE (only migration 245's trigger, a different write path, re-admits a row). An IS DISTINCT FROM guard on a NULL-scoped row compares against nothing and is vacuous by construction, not merely unnecessary — the genuinely unguarded write is the CORRECT mechanic here, same class of finding as link_massing's E1 precedent (guard:"none" is right, not merely tolerated).
compute_centroids.commit: C1 pilot 6 commit 7 (2026-08-29) — this descriptor's own introducing commit
compute_centroids.adjudicated_by: operator ruling 2026-08-29 (pilot 6 Fold C/D, B-1/S-1, Rule 9)

fixture_grandfathered_snapshot.why: The schema's own exemplar for the V7 grandfathered-unguarded shape (refresh-snapshot.js:535 — ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date) DO UPDATE with no change guard, so a same-day re-run overwrites the row in place). It is a FIXTURE, never a runnable step, and it exists so src/tests/step-schema.logic.test.ts can prove the declaration is expressible. Listing it here keeps the enforcer's GREEN direction real: without an entry the fixture would be refused, and the only way to make the suite pass would be to weaken the rule.
fixture_grandfathered_snapshot.adjudicated_by: Spec 122 V7 (schema fixture, not a manifest step)
